basis: Direct visual inspection of the fixed image; no pixel metrics.

issues: All five samples share pale, smooth shading; the glossy rubber ring especially resembles molded plastic.
Labels provide stronger material identification than appearance.
Bare metal lacks a distinct metallic reflection response; concrete looks smooth; glass/light appears opaque and unlit.
Surfaces have nearly identical color and finish, with little visible texture or roughness variation.
Samples and labels are readable, but the platform extends beyond both side edges.
Perspective and silhouettes establish depth, but similar object and platform values weaken separation.
Broad soft illumination reveals shape, but offers limited reflection contrast for distinguishing materials.
Contact shadows generally ground the samples; several broad bases have weak edge contrast.
No visible atmospheric gradient; the compact material display does not clearly require one.
Clean simplified forms support an ACG presentation, but the shared smooth finish undermines the intended industrial material vocabulary.

bounded_semantic_actions.recommendation: Trial a small, material-specific increase on concrete and painted metal; compare against this image without globally adding noise.
Trial a modest lateral shift of the key light to strengthen grazing highlights and distinguish surface response.
Pull back slightly if showing the full platform is desired.

separate_material_plan_review: Confirm bare-metal reflectance and concrete surface structure.
Confirm the intended rubber finish before reducing its prominent glossy highlights.

Specify whether glass/light should transmit light, emit light, or contain separate glass and luminous elements. Its opaque appearance requires material-plan review; roughness variation alone cannot fix it.
Establish distinct material colors and baseline finishes before further lighting adjustments.
